_note: Original to Arda. Slots are filled from the simulated society; see src/hooks/*.rs for which slots each kind receives.

variants: The Guild's Price
{guild} want what {court} will not give. {reason} The {master} is quietly hiring swords to guard the guildhall, and the {lord} wants to know who is paying them.
Stalls Shut
The {lord} has doubled the market dues, and {guild} answer by shutting their stalls. {reason} Someone has to carry terms between the {master} and the hall before the quarrel becomes a riot.
Ledgers and Lords
A ledger proving the {lord} skims the levy has gone missing from the strongroom of {guild}. {reason} The {master} will pay handsomely for its return; the {lord} will pay more for its burning.
Old Grudges
{reason} The {a_leader} wants proof that {b} are behind a string of small sabotages, and the {b_leader} swears it is the other way round.
A Meeting on Neutral Ground
{reason} Both {a} and {b} have asked strangers to witness a meeting at neutral ground, and both plan to bring more friends than agreed.
Coin for Names
{reason} The {a_leader} is offering coin for names, while the {b_leader} is offering more coin for silence.
Knives After Dark
A body in the gutter wears the token of {b}. {reason} {settlement} holds its breath to see whether {a} strike back.
The Old Banner
Old loyalties to {former} stir in {settlement}, taken only in {year}. Someone is painting the old banner on the walls at night, and the {lord} wants names.
Divided Loyalties
A pedlar from {former} is carrying letters to families in {settlement} who have kin across the border. The {lord}, who has held the place since {year}, suspects a plot to hand it back.
Whose Pasture?
Herdsmen from {other} in {foe} keep grazing across the border on the {road_class} to {settlement}. The {captain} needs someone to mark the old boundary before the next quarrel turns to killing.
The Mill Charter
{foe} claims the mill on the {road_class} to {other} is theirs by an old charter. The {captain} wants that charter found, or forged.
The Front Line
{foe} troops have been seen on the {road_class} from {other}. The {captain} needs scouts who can count banners and come back alive.
Banners on the Road
Refugees from {other} are crowding into {settlement} ahead of the {foe} army. The {captain} suspects a spy among them.
The Closed Road

{foe} has closed the {road_class} to {other}, and wagons rot at the barrier. The merchants of {settlement} will pay well for anyone who can get a caravan through, and the {captain} will look the other way.
Tolls Tripled
Tolls on the {road_class} to {other} have tripled overnight by order of {foe}. Somebody in {settlement} is profiting from the blockade, and the {captain} wants to know who.
The Bandit Road
Carts on the {km} km {road_class} to {other} keep vanishing. The {captain} suspects a band hiding in {hideout} and offers a bounty per head.
An Arrow in the Shoulder
A carter staggers into {settlement} with an arrow in his shoulder, the third this season on the {road_class} to {other}. The trail leads towards {hideout}.
The Toll-Keeper's Purse
The toll-keeper on the {road_class} to {other} has grown rich too quickly. The {captain} thinks he sells travellers' routes to the band in {hideout}.
Scarcity
{settlement} {shortfall}. Prices have tripled; the {lord} blames hoarders, and the hoarders blame the roads.
Short Measures
A shipment of {good} promised to {settlement} never arrived, and people are restless. The {lord} wants it found and the thief hanged.
Rotting in the Barns
Barns in {settlement} are bursting with {good} that nobody within reach will buy. Whoever opens a new market for it earns the {lord}'s gratitude, and the envy of every rival.
A Fixed Price
With {good} piling up unsold, the {lord} has banned its sale below a fixed price. Smugglers are already moving it out by night.
Night Cargo
{gang} run untaxed cargo past the quays at night. The {harbourmaster} is either blind or bought, and someone wants to know which.
Not Wine but Weapons
A crate dropped from a lighter split open on the quay at {settlement}: not wine but weapons. {gang} want it back before the {harbourmaster} asks questions.
Lights in the Ruins
Lights have been seen in the ruins of {ruin}, a {kind} abandoned in {year}. The {lord} wants to know who is living there before winter.
The Empty {kind}
Children from {settlement} dared each other into the ruins of {ruin}. One came back with an old silver coin and a fever; one has not come back at all.
Unquiet Graves
{years} years after {event}, the {priest} still keeps the list of the dead. Someone has begun digging in the old burial pits.
The Stranger's Gift
Survivors of {event} say the troubles began with a stranger's gift. {years} years on, the same gift has turned up again, and the {priest} is frightened.
Knocking Below
Miners refuse to go below since knocking was heard behind the galleries sealed in {year}. The {overseer} needs the seam worked before the ore wagons come.
The Old Workings
A new vein breaks into old workings nobody has records of, from before {year}. The {overseer} wants it surveyed before anyone else hears of it.
Riders by Night
{grievance} The {lord} of House {house} has been receiving riders at night, and the crown's agent in {settlement} wants to know from where.
A Lord of Two Minds
{grievance} House {house} has quietly stopped sending its levy. The {lord} insists it was bandits.
Gone Missing
A shepherd's child has not come home, and the {lord} has more pressing matters. The family begs strangers for help.
Not Home by Dark
The miller's apprentice vanished the night the river rose. The {lord} says he ran off; his mother does not believe it.
The Stranger at {place}
A stranger with a sealed letter waits every evening at {place}, asking after someone who died years ago. The {lord} would like the stranger gone.
Coins of No King
A traveller at {place} pays in coins minted by no living ruler. Word reaches the {lord} before the coins are spent.
An Ill Omen
A two-headed calf was born in {settlement} on the eve of the equinox, and the folk want a wise one to say what it means. The {lord} wants it kept quiet.
Signs and Wonders
Every dog in {settlement} howled at the same hour three nights running. The {lord} has sent for anyone who knows about such things.
The Moved Stone
Someone moved the boundary stone between {settlement} and {other} in the night. Both sides have fetched cudgels, and the {lord} needs a neutral judge.
Where the Fields Meet
A well dug on the line between {settlement} and {other} has struck something buried and worked. Both villages claim it, and the {lord} wants it seen first.
War with {other}
{style} is at war with {other}. {ruler} needs a company to hold a river crossing until the levies arrive.
A Secret Truce
{other_ruler} has offered a secret truce, carried by a single envoy who must reach {ruler} at {seat} alive. Half the court would rather the war went on.
Envoys Turned Away
Envoys from {other} were turned away at {seat}. {ruler} wants proof that {other_ruler} is paying brigands to raid the border.
The Escaped Hostage
A noble hostage from {other} has escaped from {seat}. {ruler} wants them back before {other_ruler} learns of it.
The Border Is Shut
{other} has shut its border roads to wagons from {realm}. {ruler} needs the blockade broken, or bribed open, before the harvest rots.
Wagons Turned Back
{other_ruler} has closed the border to carts from {realm}, and the carters' guild is threatening to march on {seat}. {ruler} needs proof the blockade breaks an old treaty.
The Envoy's Road
The {pact} between {realm} and {other} is up for renewal, and someone has tried to poison the envoy. Escort the new one safely to {other_ruler}.
Terms of the {pact_title}
A clause in the {pact} with {other} has been found altered in the archives at {seat}. {ruler} wants to know who benefits.
The Stolen Portrait
{ruler} seeks a marriage alliance with {other}, but the portrait sent ahead was stolen on the road.
Gifts from {other}
{other_ruler} has sent gifts to {seat}. {ruler}'s counsellors cannot agree whether they are a courtship or a bribe.
The Failing Crown
{ruler} has reigned {years} years and is failing. {claimant} is gathering friends at court, and the great houses are choosing sides.
Heirs and Claimants
A will naming the heir of {ruler} has vanished from the chapel at {seat}. {claimant} swears to know nothing of it.
The Levy Unpaid
{vassal} has stopped sending the levy. {grievance} {ruler} wants to know whether it is sulking or rebellion.
A Lord in Revolt
{vassal} has closed the gates to the crown's tax-gatherers. {grievance} {ruler} needs a go-between before blood is spilt.
Fever on the Roads
A sickness like {plague} of {years} years ago is being reported on the roads. {ruler} wants its source found before panic spreads.
Opened Graves
Old graves from {plague} have been opened in the night. The folk of {realm} whisper that someone wants the sickness back.
The Buried Charter
Scholars at {seat} believe {ruin}, a {kind} near {near} settled in {year}, hides records that could undo House {house}'s right to rule.
Treasure-Hunters
Treasure-hunters are digging at {ruin}, near {near}. {ruler} wants them stopped, or wants a share.
The Tax Strike
{ruler} takes {tax} in every hundred on trade, about {levy} sp a year, and the towns grumble. A pamphleteer calling for a tax strike must be found, or protected, depending on who pays.
The Stolen Rolls
The crown's tax rolls for {realm} were stolen on the way to {seat}. Every town is suddenly very quiet.
The Royal Progress
{ruler} will tour {realm} this summer. Every lord is scrambling to impress, and somebody would like the progress to end early.
The Ruler in Disguise
{ruler} is travelling from {seat} in disguise to see the realm unguarded, and needs discreet companions.
Counting Hearths
The crown has ordered a count of every hearth in {realm}, and the census-takers keep being run out of villages.
The Missing Census-Taker
A census-taker has gone missing between {seat} and the hills, and so have the rolls he carried.
The Great Tourney
A great tourney is called at {seat}. Riders arrive from every corner of {realm}, and they bring their old feuds with them.
A Poisoned Champion
The champion of the last tourney at {seat} was found poisoned. {ruler} wants the culprit before the next bout.
An Old Claim Revived
{former} never formally gave up its claim to {settlement}, lost in {year}. An envoy has arrived with a mouldering charter and a lawyer, and the {lord} wants the charter proved a forgery.
The Charter of {former}
A family in {settlement} has produced a deed from before {year}, when the place belonged to {former}, claiming half the common fields. The {lord} needs the truth before the next quarter-day.
Trade War
{ruler} has closed the roads to {other} to punish {other_ruler}; smugglers on both sides are growing rich, and one of them knows too much.
The Closed Border
By order of {ruler}, no wagon may cross into {other}. The merchants of {seat} are quietly paying anyone who can get their goods through regardless.
A Crown Contested
{ruler} came to power only {years} years ago, and {claimant} has never accepted it. Letters are passing between the claimant and lords who remember the old house.
The Old Blood
{claimant} is holding a feast for the lords of {realm} on the anniversary of the old house's fall. {ruler} wants someone inside.
Dues Unpaid
{reason} The {master} wants a champion to argue their case before the {lord} at the next court day, and the {lord} wants the ringleaders named.
The Bailiff's Seizure
{reason} Now the {lord}'s bailiff has seized the tools of three of them, and the {master} is talking of burning the tally sticks.
By Order of the Crown
{ruler} has closed the {road_class} to {other} in {foe}, and wagons stand idle in {settlement}. The {captain} is under orders to turn back every cart, and under pressure to let a few through.
The Embargo
Nothing may cross into {foe} on the {road_class} to {other}, by order of {ruler}. Somebody in {settlement} is running goods over the fields at night, and the {captain} is expected to catch them.
A Wolf Winter
Something is taking sheep from the high pastures above {settlement}, and the tracks are too large for any wolf. The {lord} has promised a fleece and a silver penny for its head.
The Last Shepherd
A shepherd from {settlement} came down from the {terrain} raving about eyes in the dark and refuses to go back. The flock is still up there.
Rising Water
The river is higher than it has been since {flood}, and the old dyke above {settlement} is weeping. The {lord} needs hands to shore it, and someone to find out who has been cutting the dyke at night.
The Drowned Fields
Silt from {flood} buried a boundary stone, and now two families of {settlement} claim the same field. The {lord} wants the stone dug up before the ploughing.
The Levy
{realm} is calling up its levies, and {settlement} owes {men} men. The {lord} is short, and strangers passing through look like a solution.
Deserters
Men who ran from the last muster of {realm} are hiding in the woods near {settlement}. The {lord} is ordered to bring them in; their families are feeding them.
Fair Day
The yearly fair at {settlement} draws pedlars, players and pickpockets from every road. The {lord} wants the peace kept, and a travelling troupe wants protection from someone it will not name.
The Harvest Feast
At the harvest feast in {settlement} the best ale goes missing, and so does the brewer. The {lord} wants both back before the toasts.
What the Plough Turned Up
A ploughman near {settlement} has turned up a sealed stone box. The {lord} claims it by right of the land; the ploughman has already hidden it.
Bones in the Field
Old bones and a rusted crown came up with the spring ploughing at {settlement}. Folk want them reburied before anyone asks whose they are; the {lord} wants them shown to scholars.
A Wedding Feud
Two families of {settlement} are to be joined at midsummer, and neither can stand the other. The {lord} needs the wedding to go ahead without blood.
The Runaway Bride
A bride from {settlement} has run off the night before her wedding, with the dowry. The {lord} would rather she were found quietly.
